question: Will Russia enter Stavky by September 30?
rules:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if, according to the ISW map, Russia captures any territory of Stavky, Donetsk Oblast, (49.048958° N, 37.829063° E) between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET.

Territory will be considered captured if any part of the specified territory is shaded under a below specified layer on the ISW map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) by the resolution date. Otherwise, the market will resolve to “No”.

The boundaries of the municipality are those shown under the “Ukrainian Settlements” layer on the ISW map.

For any change on the ISW map to qualify for this market’s resolution, the relevant shading must persist through the next full ISW daily update cycle. If ISW skips a day, shading must persist until the next finalized ISW update is published, regardless of the date.

Any continuous shading under the following layers will qualify:
- Assessed Russian Infiltration Areas
- Assessed Russian-Controlled Terrain
- Assessed Russian Advances

Shading under the following layers will not qualify:
- Claimed Russian Territory

Once a qualifying condition is met, any subsequent loss of control will not be considered

evidence.publisher: Institute for the Study of War
evidence.excerpt: Russian forces continued offensive operations toward Lyman itself on September 16 to 17 but did not advance as Ukrainian forces counterattacked in the area. Ukrainian 3rd Army Corps Commander Brigadier General Andrii Biletskyi stated on September 17 that Ukrainian forces operationally defeated the Russian northern pincer in the Lyman direction and that Operation Vivaldi continues.

evidence.publisher: Institute for the Study of War
evidence.excerpt: There has been mixed reporting that Russian forces may maintain limited positions in some areas of the salient north of Lyman, including near Shandryholove, Stavky, Derylove, and Ridkodub. The full extent of Ukrainian advances in the Lyman direction and the shape of the frontline in the area remains unclear, due to limited open-source evidence about the salient.

evidence.publisher: Institute for the Study of War
evidence.excerpt: Ukrainian 3rd Army Corps Commander Brigadier General Andrii Biletskyi confirmed on September 15 that Ukrainian forces have been conducting a counteroffensive — Operation Vivaldi — against the Russian salient north of Lyman. Biletskyi stated that Ukrainian forces have cleared or liberated a total of 85 square kilometers, including liberating Serednie and clearing Russian infiltrators from Novoselivka, Yarova, Oleksandrivka, and the outskirts of Korovii Yar. Russian forces continued offensive operations in the Lyman direction on September 14 and 15 but did not advance.

evidence.publisher: Institute for the Study of War
evidence.excerpt: Russian milbloggers claimed on September 9 through 11 that Ukrainian forces had effectively cut the Russian salient north of Lyman and pushed Russian forces to the Zherebets River. One Russian milblogger, who acknowledged that the Russian salient was essentially gone, claimed that fighting is still ongoing in some areas within the salient, including near Shandryholove, Stavky, Derylove, and Ridkodub. Some individual Russian elements may still be operating within the former salient as Ukrainian forces continue to clear the area.

Biletskyi said Ukrainian troops had cleared 75 square kilometers in northern Donetsk Oblast of Russian infiltrators and liberated 10 square kilometers, including the village of Serednie. In the Lyman counterattacks, months of Russian infiltrations meant that in addition to moving forward and taking territory, Ukrainian forces also had to systematically clear the rear area of Russian infiltration groups. The areas Biletskyi announced as cleared or liberated on Sept. 15 — Oleksandrivka, Yarova, Korovii Yar, and Novoselivka — mostly saw this type of operation and never fully left Ukrainian control according to most open-source maps.

evidence.publisher: Ukrinform, citing the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine
evidence.excerpt: Ukrinform reports this, citing operational information from the General Staff as of 10 p.m. on September 15, 2026, posted on Facebook. In the Lyman direction, our defenders successfully repelled six attempts by the invaders to advance near Novoselivka, Drobysheve, Stavky, Lyman, and Dibrova; another combat engagement is ongoing.
